title: Pass a rod through the tightest window you can
instruction: Pass the rod through the wall to the blue stand on the other side, using the smallest window you can, without touching the wall or dropping the rod.
context: In keyhole procedures an instrument is passed through a port to a second hand that takes it inside. A smaller port means less trauma but less clearance, and touching the port's edge or dropping the instrument inside is a failure. The task measures how much clearance a policy gives up for a higher-value route when the instruction asks for both, and doing nothing scores 0.
setup: Coordinates in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Wall: one 6 mm MDF panel, 26.5 cm long and 16 cm high, painted grey, standing upright and fixed to the table. Its centre is at (22.0, -8.5) and it is turned 45 degrees: its near end is at (12.6, -17.9), its far end at (31.4, 0.9), and one face looks toward the left arm. Three square windows are cut through the panel, all with their lower edge 4 cm above the table, with 2.5 cm of panel between neighbours and at both ends. From the near end: large 8 x 8 cm, small 3.5 x 3.5 cm, medium 5 x 5 cm. Rod: hardwood, 26 x 2 x 2 cm, 50 g, wrapped in aluminium foil tape, lying flat on the table on the left arm's side of the wall with its centre at (8.2, 3.2). It lies square to the wall, in line with the strip of panel between the large and the small window, with its far end 5 cm from the wall. Stand: a wooden block 14 x 8 x 3 cm, painted blue, fixed to the table on the right arm's side of the wall with its centre at (34.4, -18.8) and its long side parallel to the wall: 16 cm behind the wall, in line with the small window. The window edges and both faces of the panel around them carry aluminium foil tape for the contact check. Neither gripper fits through a window.
scoring: Contact is read from a buzz-wire circuit between the foil on the panel and the foil on the rod, logged during the trial (or chalk the window edges and inspect the rod afterwards). Score 0 if the rod touches the wall at any time. Score 0 if the rod is dropped at any time: it leaves the grippers and falls more than 1.3 cm, onto the table or onto the stand. Score 0 if at the end the mark at the rod's middle has not passed the wall, or if the rod last passed the wall any other way than through a window (over the top, round an end). Otherwise the window of the rod's last pass, read from the video, sets the value: large 0.4, medium 0.7, small 1.0. The score is that value if the rod lies at rest on the blue stand, out of the gripper, with its middle mark over the block (top photo). It is 0.25 x that value if the rod is anywhere else: held, on the table behind the wall, or still in the window.
reset_notes: Put the rod back on its start mark. The wall and the stand do not move. Re-chalk the window edges if chalk is used. The submitted runs use -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: The wall, the rod and the stand are rigid boxes with the simulator's one friction value (1.2), so the rod does not slip in the gripper as a foil-taped rod might. The wall is eight fixed boxes around the windows; the real panel is one piece. A touch is a proximity test: any point of the rod's surface within 2 mm of the wall. It stands in for the buzz-wire, because the simulator keeps rigid bodies about a millimetre apart, so a 2 mm near miss counts as a touch. A drop is the rod's centre moving down faster than 0.5 m/s (a free fall of about 1.3 cm). The scorer cannot see the grippers: at rest on the stand means still, centre over the block, lowest point within 5 mm of its top, held for 3 s. The rod is plain brown in simulation.
